hypotheses.justification: `hM` occurs neither in the statement nor in the proof. The only appearance of `M` in the conclusion is inside `ModularCurve.igusaFunctionFieldX1C k M w` (which needs only `[Field k]` and `w : IntegralWeightOneForm k M`), so `hM` can be dropped and the very same proof term still typechecks.
`hpM` is never mentioned in the statement or in the proof; nothing else has a type depending on it. Deleting it leaves the conclusion literally unchanged, so the same proof goes through.

`hζ` is not used in the proof and does not appear in the conclusion (`ζ` occurs only in the type of `hζ`). Deleting it leaves an unused binder `(ζ : L)`, which is harmless, so the statement stays true with the same proof. (`ζ` itself cannot be deleted on its own, since the type of `hζ` mentions it.)

`hK` is unused: the conclusion and the proof only use `K` through the given instances `[Algebra A ↥K]`, `[IsScalarTower A L ↥K]` and `ModularCurve.TwoChart.modelTo A (↥K) j`. Nothing rewrites along `hK`, so removal does not change the statement and the same proof works.
`hAp` does not occur in the statement or the proof. It is a plain `Prop` argument (not an instance), so its removal cannot affect elaboration either; the same proof applies verbatim.

hypotheses.binder: (hζA : ∃ z : A, algebraMap A L z = ζ)
hypotheses.justification: `hζA` is an explicit `Prop` argument, unused in the proof and absent from the conclusion. Deleting it does not affect any instance search (the `Algebra A L` instance it needs is a separate binder that is kept), so the statement remains provable by the same proof.

`hj` is never used: `j` occurs in the statement only through `ModularCurve.TwoChart.modelTo A (↥K) j` and `ModularCurve.TwoChart.ιFin A (↥K) j`, which require only `[Fact (j ≠ 0)]` (kept). Deleting `hj` thus leaves the conclusion unchanged and the same proof compiles.

hypotheses.binder: (hcover : ∀ z : ↥(pullback (ModularCurve.TwoChart.modelTo A (↥K) j) (specMap A k)), z ∈ Set.range i₁.1.base ∨ z ∈ Set.range i₂.1.base)
hypotheses.justification: `hcover` is not used anywhere in the proof and does not occur in the conclusion. It is an explicit `Prop` hypothesis, so removing it does not break elaboration; the statement stays true by the identical proof. (The two-chart cover is never invoked: the proof produces its good points pointwise via `GenChartTools.good_point`.)

`hred` is never referenced in the proof and is absent from the conclusion. Since it is an explicit `Prop` argument, its presence is not needed for typeclass synthesis either (reducedness of the intersection plays no role: only the finiteness of `Set.range (pullback.fst i₁.1 i₂.1).base`, obtained from `hn`/`hn0`, is used). Removal leaves the statement true with the same proof.

Instance-implicit and derived from nothing: `p` is still an argument (through `[CharP k p]`, `(hpM)`, `(hAp)`), but no remaining binder, no definition in the conclusion (`igusaFunctionFieldX1C`, `Pic0`, `TwoChart.modelTo`, `ιFin`, `SchemeHomOver`, `Divisor.degZero`) and no step of the proof requires `Fact p.Prime` (cf. the definition of `IntegralWeightOneForm`/`igusaFunctionFieldX1C`, which only need `[Field κ]` and `M`). Deleting it leaves the statement literally identical and the same proof compiles.

`M` only appears in `ModularCurve.igusaFunctionFieldX1C k M w`; by `Def_ModularCurve_IgusaFunctionFieldX1` this is `IgusaCover.igusaFunctionField (x1FunctionFieldC κ M) w.hasseRootFn`, and `x1FunctionFieldC κ M = qExpFunctionFieldC κ (Gamma1 M)` needs no `NeZero M` (`Gamma1` and `ModularForm` are defined for all `M`; `NeZero` is only required for the finite-index instance, which is not used here). The proof never uses it, so the statement remains true and provable.

`L` occurs in the conclusion only through the type of `K` (`IntermediateField L (LaurentSeries L)`), which needs `[Field L]` (kept) but no characteristic-zero assumption. `CharZero L` is not used in the proof, so deletion preserves the statement and the proof.

Nothing in the conclusion refers to `L` except the type `K : IntermediateField L (LaurentSeries L)`, and the proof never uses the cyclotomic hypothesis. Removing this instance-implicit argument leaves the statement unchanged and the same proof term still elaborates.

After keeping `[CommRing A]` and `[IsDomain A]` (the two parameters of the class `IsDiscreteValuationRing`, see `Mathlib/RingTheory/DiscreteValuationRing/Basic.lean`), no remaining hypothesis or definition uses the discrete-valuation structure: `A` appears in the conclusion only via `ModularCurve.TwoChart.modelTo A (↥K) j` and `specMap A k`, which need `[CommRing A]`, `[Algebra A ↥K]`, `[Algebra A k]`. The proof never uses the valuation. Hence the argument can be deleted.

Unused in the statement (`L`/`A` are related in the conclusion only through `[Algebra A ↥K]`, `[Algebra A k]` and `modelTo`) and unused in the proof. Deleting it leaves an unchanged conclusion provable by the same proof.

The conclusion only needs `[Algebra A ↥K]` (for `ModularCurve.TwoChart.modelTo A (↥K) j` and the two-chart model), which is a separate binder that is kept; the scalar-tower compatibility is never used in the statement or in the proof. Hence it can be deleted without changing the conclusion, and the same proof still works.

The characteristic assumption is never used: the conclusion mentions `k` only through `[Field k]`, `Spec (CommRingCat.of k)`, `specMap A k`, `Pic0 k ↥(...)` and `Divisor.degZero (K := k)`, and the proof only uses `[IsAlgClosed k]`, `Mdl₁`'s own instances and the abstract lemma `AlgebraicCurve.Pic0.mem_closure_mk_single_sub_single_of_notMem` (which requires only `[Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]`). `p` remains an argument via the other hypotheses, so deleting `[CharP k p]` leaves a well-typed statement that is proved by the same argument.
